adaptation_1_activities.name: Tap that sound
adaptation_1_activities.description: Children can keep sticky notes with the sound on it. Before beginning a new lesson have children stick some of their sound cards on their desk. The teacher provides the sound and children tap the correct sound card.

adaptation_1_activities.name: Sound Spark
adaptation_1_activities.description: The teacher points to a sound card and children must chorally pronounce the sound.

adaptation_1_activities.name: Sound Detective
adaptation_1_activities.description: Children focus on listening to the beginning, middle, or end sound. The teacher says a word and indicates to children where in the word they should listen for that sound. Children then point to the correct sound.

adaptation_1_activities.name: Write the sound
adaptation_1_activities.description: The teacher says a sound, and children write the letter that corresponds to that sound on a mini whiteboard. This can also be done with writing the sound at the beginning, middle, and end for more advanced students.

adaptation_1_activities.name: How many sounds
adaptation_1_activities.description: The teacher says a word. Children use a manipulative to count and show how many sounds. This activity should be used for children at more advanced stages of phonemic awareness.

adaptation_1_activities.name: Sort the sound
adaptation_1_activities.description: The teacher says a sound and children sort by either voiced or unvoiced, continuous or stops.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Sound Hunt
adaptation_2_activities.description: Teacher says words; children must listen to beginning, middle, or end sound to identify the target phoneme. Children can indicate that they hear target sound by lifting a card with the target sound.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Hide-and-Seek Sound
adaptation_2_activities.description: Teacher says words that have the target sound in different positions; it could be at the beginning, middle, or end position. Children must find where the sound is by holding up a beginning, middle, or end card.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Chop-a-Sound
adaptation_2_activities.description: Children are given words with the target sound. They either chop the target sound or another previously learned sound and say what is left.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Sound Puzzle
adaptation_2_activities.description: Children are given two previously learned sounds at a time; they must add in the target sound to create a word.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Sound Switch-a-Roo
adaptation_2_activities.description: Children are given words that include previously learned sounds. They are asked to change a beginning, middle, or end sound by substituting in the new sound.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Spell Aloud
adaptation_2_activities.description: Teacher takes previously sound patterns of words and asks children to change a sound to the target sound and spell aloud.

adaptation_2_activities.name: Silly Sentence
adaptation_2_activities.description: Teacher asks children to think of words that contain the target sound or sound pattern. Then collaboratively build a sentence using as many of those words as possible.

adaptation_2_activities.name: How Many Sounds
adaptation_2_activities.description: Teacher provides children with words that include previously learned sounds and the target sound. Children must segment the sounds in each word.

level_1_motor_foundation.name: Finger Run
level_1_motor_foundation.description: Children run their finger from left to right across the handwriting lines, pointing to the top, middle, and bottom lines as the teacher names them.

level_1_motor_foundation.name: Magic Finger Write
level_1_motor_foundation.description: Children use their 'magic' pointer finger to trace letter shapes on the lines, following the teacher's modeling and verbal stroke cues.

level_1_motor_foundation.name: Sky Writing
level_1_motor_foundation.description: With big arm movements, children write letters in the air while saying the strokes aloud, using shoulders and elbows to build motor memory.

level_1_motor_foundation.name: Bumpy Road Letters
level_1_motor_foundation.description: Children trace textured letter cards (made from sandpaper or raised paint) with their fingers, following the correct stroke path by feel.

level_2_guided_formation.name: Trace & Say
level_2_guided_formation.description: Children trace letters on dotted-line templates with a pencil, saying the strokes aloud.

level_2_guided_formation.name: Start Dot Letters
level_2_guided_formation.description: Letters are printed with start dots and arrows. Children follow the marks to complete each letter step-by-step.

level_2_guided_formation.name: Rainbow Write
level_2_guided_formation.description: Children trace the same letter multiple times with different colored pencils, following correct formation for each layer.

level_2_guided_formation.name: Letter Ladder
level_2_guided_formation.description: A visual with steps for each part of the letter. Children write each step, climbing the 'ladder' to finish the full letter.

level_3_semi_independent.name: Top to Bottom Challenge
level_3_semi_independent.description: Children write letters using correct formation, earning a star or check each time they start at the top and follow the correct stroke order.

level_3_semi_independent.name: Line Talkers
level_3_semi_independent.description: Children describe how the letter touches the lines.

level_3_semi_independent.name: Cover & Try
level_3_semi_independent.description: Children trace a letter, then cover the model and try writing it on their own, focusing on correct sequence and placement.

level_3_semi_independent.name: Letter Coach
level_3_semi_independent.description: Children work in pairs—one child 'coaches' by checking if the other starts in the right place and follows the stroke order, using friendly reminders.

adaptation_4_activities.name: Trace the Sound You Hear
adaptation_4_activities.description: Teacher says a sound, but includes multiple opportunities for children to hear the target sound, and children trace the matching letter or letter pattern.

adaptation_4_activities.name: Write the Sound You Hear
adaptation_4_activities.description: Teacher says a sound, and children write the matching letter or letter pattern.

adaptation_4_activities.name: Sound-Letter Hunt
adaptation_4_activities.description: Teacher says words; children must listen to either the beginning, middle, or end sound to identify the target phoneme. Children then write the corresponding sound they hear.

adaptation_4_activities.name: Mystery Word Builder
adaptation_4_activities.description: Teacher gives sounds one at a time, and children write each sound as they hear it to form a word. Then they blend and read the completed word.

adaptation_4_activities.name: Sound Switch Writing
adaptation_4_activities.description: Children write a simple word, then change one sound when prompted to create a new word. Focus should be on the target letter-sound.

adaptation_4_activities.name: What's that Pattern
adaptation_4_activities.description: Teacher provides children with words that include previously learned sounds and the target sound. Children must segment the sounds in each word and write the corresponding letter or letter patterns.
